description:
Record your result, return it to the calling agent and finish.

For a purchase assignment, `completed` means the merchant confirmed the order or booking. Use it only after reading that confirmation. Put the evidence and any confirmation number in `summary`; this report also records the purchase. You do not need to repeat the confirmation in other fields. For a review assignment, `completed` means the requested cart is ready and Muse has confirmed it; no order is implied.

For an attempted order, use `outcome: not_placed` for positive evidence that it failed, such as a payment rejection, and `outcome: unknown` when the pages you can read do not settle it. Explain the evidence in `summary`. An empty order history or a return to checkout does not prove failure.

If recording remains unavailable, report `blocked` with what the merchant showed and what remains unresolved in `summary`. Leave out `outcome` and `confirmation` to hand back the existing records. A recording error does not mean the order failed; do not repeat the submission or keep retrying the same failed record.

Include orders the user completed while controlling the browser. Successful funding, a pressed button, or an accepted request does not prove completion.

Use `needs_input` when an unresolved fact or decision must return to Muse, and `blocked` when no permitted route remains or Muse asks you to stop. Choose one of these statuses when a purchase ends without a confirmed order, including when an item is unavailable. Include `reason` when a listed label fits. In `summary`, include the submitted details, any changed total, outstanding work and relevant evidence. If the merchant's outcome remains unresolved, say so and describe the remaining verification. Leave out tool transcripts, secrets, raw page text and instructions for other agents.

url.description: With open: the page to load in the new tab.

tab.description: With select and close: the tab. With open and ref: the tab whose latest view shows the link.

ref.description: With open, in place of url: a link's element reference from the tab's latest view. The page the link leads to opens in the new tab.
